text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Israel on alert for more attacks: Cabinet stops short of suspending talks as Arafat accused of giving green light to militants.
- Autopsies seek clues to deadly ritual: five bodies found in Quebec house.
- Hospitals map war against superbugs: Quarantine plan to be weighed.
- EU weighs aid force for Albania: President may have helped create chaos in order to protect own position.
- UN seeks to bring justice to Cambodia: When a judge admits he knows little about the law, reform is difficult.
- Manning gets friendly with urban Ontario: In its drive to be more than a regional party of protest, Reform wants seats in Oshawa and communities like it.
- Bank of Canada faces rates test: Analysts believe central bank will resist following expected U.S. Fed hike.
- Beland warns of risk from Desjardins rivals: Says big banks pose threat to caisses' survival.
- 'What's good for Gazprom is good for Russia': The once state-owned giant is secretive, powerful - and one of richest companies in the world.
- Analysts foresee cure for ailing drug shares.
- All-star analysts: The post picks seven to watch.
- Bre-X pounded as Busang rumors swirl: Shares tumble on report that gold find is much smaller than estimated.
- Outlook getting gloomier for Repap B.C. creditors.
